scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Entanglement with zero distillable secret key in local dimension ten” (preprints/Entanglement-with-zero-distillable-secret-key-in-local-dimension-ten-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 272 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 be18f63c5a1d11a2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an explicitly specified entangled density operator ρ on C10 ⊗ C10 whose range contains no nonzero product vector and for which KD(ρ) = 0. More precisely, let n ≥ 1 and let τKAKBE′ be the normalized output of any admitted completed bit-output protocol of Definition 4.1 on ρ⊗n, where E′ retains an initial purification and the complete public transcript. For every state σE′ , τKAKBE′ − 1 2 1 X i=0 |i, i⟩⟨i, i| ⊗ σE′ 1 ≥ 1 5 . (1.1) Thus the corresponding trace distance, with its conventional factor 1/2, is at least 1/10.
